name: Thomas Wolsey
role: Lord Chancellor of England (1515–1529) and Catholic cardinal
summary: Wolsey served as Henry VIII’s chief minister and negotiated the 1518 Treaty of London. He used his ecclesiastical authority to reorganize religious foundations and endow colleges.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Wolsey’s dispatches in 1521 record his ministry’s preparations to deploy English forces by land and sea in conjunction with negotiations for a joint war against France.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Wolsey obtained the 1514 subsidy on income from wages and land and later fixed rates applicable to wages, salaries and income from land in his instructions for the 1525 levy.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Wolsey issued expenditure warrants directly through the royal chamber. His administration funded the opening of the 1521 war without a parliamentary grant, using compulsory loans before Parliament met in 1523.

church-by-bishops.rationale: As papal legate, Wolsey issued nationwide directions through the diocesan bishops, commissioning them to enforce the church’s 1521 prohibition on Lutheran books in their jurisdictions.

collective-defense.rationale: Wolsey designed and signed the 1518 Treaty of London, which provided for joint military action by the other signatories against an aggressor that refused to restore the peace.

decide-locally.rationale: Wolsey made the response to grain shortages a nationwide program, extending the grain-search commissions from selected localities to every county. He gave commissioners authority to send those who resisted compulsory sales to London for punishment.

harm-principle.rationale: Wolsey’s legatine mandate of 1521 ordered the surrender and destruction of Lutheran books and directed proceedings against people who possessed or supported them on grounds of doctrinal error.

money-backed-by-precious-metals.rationale: Wolsey headed the 1526 commission that revalued English gold and silver coinage and set revised precious-metal standards for the currency.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wolsey endowed Cardinal College with a curriculum that gave scripture and theology a central place. As papal legate he also convened an ecclesiastical court to decide the validity of Henry VIII’s marriage.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wolsey used the Crown’s Chancery to order enclosed land returned to cultivation, subject to an exception for enclosures shown to benefit the commonwealth.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Wolsey used the Crown’s Chancery and Star Chamber to adjudicate civil disputes and enforce remedies in his capacity as Lord Chancellor.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wolsey’s 1518 decree ordered landlords to pull down post-1485 enclosures and restore tillage, with a substantial fine for failure to comply unless the owners could show a public benefit.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Wolsey invoked his legatine authority to require bishops to suppress publications containing Lutheran teachings and to institute proceedings against their possessors and supporters.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wolsey exercised papal jurisdiction while serving as royal chancellor and used a papal commission to hear the king’s marriage case at Blackfriars.

state-harmful.rationale: Wolsey regularly exercised the Crown’s civil jurisdiction in Chancery and Star Chamber, hearing petitions and issuing judgments.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Richard Pace’s letter to Wolsey of 3 September 1521 records the agreement Wolsey had concluded at Bruges, binding England and the Habsburg emperor to terms for a joint war against France.

taxation-theft.rationale: Wolsey pursued a parliamentary subsidy in 1523 and formally commended the Speaker’s part in securing its passage in his 24 August letter to Henry VIII.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Wolsey helped organize the 1513 French campaign that took Tournai and then negotiated a peace in which Louis XII yielded possession of the town to England.

notes: I searched the state papers, Cavendish’s account and the documentary and scholarly sources across public finance, property, trade, food supply, government and courts, civil liberty, religion, education and culture, war and diplomacy, and the methods of political change. I checked the land and scarcity records for ecology, the education and coinage records for technology, and the alliance terms and Scottish correspondence for globalism. Enclosure policy addressed cultivation and the loss of settlements. The 1518 league provided for joint enforcement. The record I read did not establish that an outside arbitrator could impose a final award on the parties. The tax sources record a mix of income and goods assessments, and the grain measures address supply and forced sales. I also checked the alien craft statutes and the responses to the Amicable Grant protests for the gaps on ethnicity, class and political opposition. The sources attribute the 1523 craft restrictions to petitions and legislation and do not document Wolsey’s position on immigration levels or ethnic membership. I found no work authored by Wolsey in the Gutenberg catalog. The local Gutenberg Life and its appendices are by Cavendish and other contributors and include some of Wolsey’s correspondence.
